request: Analyze GSE302867 for PMID 40993371 (Cardiac adaptation to endurance exercise training requires suppression of GDF15 via PGC-1α.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk polyA RNA-seq of whole mouse heart (Illumina HiSeq2500, Novogene)
final.design: 2x2 factorial: genotype (WT vs cardiomyocyte-specific PGC-1a KO) x exercise (sedentary vs 6-week voluntary wheel running), n=5 male mice per group (Fig 2e/f, Fig 4a legends)
final.primary_estimand: Effect of 6-week voluntary wheel endurance training on the heart transcriptome within each genotype (WT_Ex vs WT_Sed; KO_Ex vs KO_Sed), Fig 2e-f
planned_contrasts: WT_Ex vs WT_Sed (Fig 2e GSEA Hallmark OXPHOS NES=5.14 FDR=8.8e-5; Fig 2f; no DEG count reported)
KO_Ex vs KO_Sed (Fig 2e GSEA OXPHOS NES=-10.22 FDR=8.2e-5; no DEG count reported)
KO_Sed vs WT_Sed (Fig 4a volcano, Gdf15 most upregulated; no DEG count reported)
KO_Ex vs WT_Ex (Fig 4a volcano, Gdf15 most upregulated; no DEG count reported)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none; each mouse contributes one heart
final.paper_method: DESeq2 (S4.10.p1); GSEA classic mode on Hallmark MH and M8 gene sets
final.paper_results: No DEG counts given in text or figure legends; GSEA OXPHOS up in WT training, depleted in KO training (FIG11 e); Gdf15 top upregulated KO vs WT in both states (S2.4.p2, FIG13 a)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S4.10.p1: DESeq2, DE if |log2FC|>1 and BH-adjusted P<0.05. FIG11 (Fig 2e-f): bulk cardiac RNA-seq n=5/group, WT_Ex vs WT_Sed and KO_Ex vs KO_Sed GSEA. FIG13 (Fig 4a): KO_Sed vs WT_Sed and KO_Ex vs WT_Ex volcano plots, DESeq2 FDR<0.05. S2.4.p2: 4 groups sequenced. DA.p1 names GSE302867. The request is the exercise effect, so the two within-genotype training contrasts are primary; the genotype contrasts are secondary.

checks: DA.p1 deposits bulk heart RNA-seq under GSE302867
GEO: Heart, Mus musculus, male, HiSeq 2500 (matches S4.10.p1), 20 samples = 4 groups x 5 (matches Fig 2e n=5/group)
sample titles WT_Sed/KO_Sed/WT_Ex/KO_Ex match the paper's group names

ownership.reasoning: Data availability statement DA.p1 names GSE302867; platform, tissue, sex, and group structure all match the paper.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns G1-1..G4-5 equal the library names in the GEO description field (inspect: 20/20 match). Group comes from the title (WT_Sed_1 etc.), which agrees with the genotype and treatment characteristics columns. Level names recoded to be formula-safe.

matrix.reasoning: File name processed_data_fpkm; GEO data_processing: featureCounts then FPKM normalization, supplementary file contains FPKM; integer fraction 0.17, max 69409, non-negative. Paper analysed counts with DESeq2, but raw counts were not deposited, so the paper's input is unavailable.

final.analysis_type: multi-group (2x2 factorial as four cell means, one model)

candidates.value: pooled Ex vs Sed across genotypes
candidates.reason_rejected: paper analyses training within each genotype and the genotypes respond in opposite directions (Fig 2e); pooling would average opposite effects
one model on all 20 samples gives a shared variance estimate and is the paper's 4-group layout

design.reasoning: Paper's exercise estimands are simple effects of training within genotype (FIG11 e); genotype effects within state are Fig 4a. One cell-means model with four planned contrasts keeps every factor level separate.

covariance.reasoning: Independent mice, one heart each; GEO batch field is a single date for all samples, sex constant male, age constant 14-16 weeks. No blocking unit.

final.method: limma (lmFit + contrasts.fit + eBayes, cell-means model on log2(FPKM+1))

paper_route.reason: GEO deposits FPKM only; raw featureCounts counts were not deposited, and FPKM must not be rounded into counts

deviations: limma on log2(FPKM+1) instead of DESeq2 on counts; fold changes are on the log2(FPKM+1) scale and are compressed for low-expression genes

method.reasoning: Matrix-method policy: FPKM -> log2(x+1) -> limma. Paper route DESeq2 blocked by missing counts.

final.deviation_note: Paper rule applied to limma on log2(FPKM+1); log2FC from log FPKM is not identical to DESeq2 shrunken/MLE log2FC

threshold.reasoning: S4.10.p1: up if log2FC>1, down if log2FC<-1, BH-adjusted P<0.05. Audit rule padj<0.05 without fold-change cutoff for comparison with Fig 4a (FDR<0.05).

caveats: paper reports no DEG counts for any contrast, so counts cannot be compared
limma on log2(FPKM+1) replaces the paper's DESeq2 on counts
paper's GSEA used DESeq2 normalized expression with phenotype permutation; ours is preranked on the limma t statistic

study.reasoning: S2.4.p2/FIG13: Gdf15 the most upregulated gene in KO vs WT in both states; Ppargc1a is the knocked-out gene (expected down). Training contrasts have only pathway-level claims (OXPHOS GSEA), checked through enrichment.

discrepancies.paper: 6 weeks voluntary wheel running for molecular analyses (S4.4.p1, FIG11)

executions.name: joint
executions.reasoning: one limma cell-means model on all 20 samples with the four planned contrasts in the paper's direction (run_joint_limma only offers KOSed_vs_KOEx / WTEx_vs_KOEx for the non-reference pairs, i.e. reversed sign); the two training contrasts are the primary exercise estimands, genotype contrasts secondary

enrichment.reasoning: paper Fig 2e: Hallmark GSEA for WT training (OXPHOS up)
paper Fig 2e: Hallmark GSEA for KO training (OXPHOS depleted)
